note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Companies promised AI gains— here's how the payoff showed up in earnings
items.blurb: Novartis, Santander and Standard Chartered credited AI in results, though most firms still cannot isolate its contribution.

items.title: Behind the Curtain: OpenAI's post-election power play
items.blurb: OpenAI plans a policy and publicity push after the midterms, including rebranding data centers as AI compute campuses.

items.title: For JPMorgan, Amazon, fighting AI bots like Meta Muse may not be a winning long-term strategy
items.blurb: JPMorgan, Amazon and Schwab block outside AI agents over security risks, though Accenture found 71% of customers want bank-app assistants.

items.title: Why AI is boosting Meta's ad business while hurting Google search
items.blurb: Meta's third-quarter ad revenue rose 26% against 12% for Google search, as chatbots pull users away from traditional search.

items.title: Everything changed for the oil, AI and bond trades over the past month
items.blurb: BlackRock's Jeffrey Rosenberg says hyperscaler spending is driving a growing wave of public bond issuance, including Microsoft's return to that market.

items.title: Anthropic's path to the Nasdaq just got a lot bumpier
items.blurb: Anthropic's filing showed an $80 billion first-half net loss, just as investors turned wary of AI spending.

items.title: Humans are still doing the work behind some AI agents
items.blurb: Agents still fail at tasks like phone calls, so startups hire people to finish the work.

items.title: AI is coming to construction sites. But does it make workers safer?
items.blurb: Firms report fewer incidents, but researchers say evidence that AI prevents injuries remains limited.

items.title: Worst ever Binance crypto hack reveals North Korea's evolving tactics
items.blurb: Speed and automation in the $6.3 billion theft raise fresh questions about how AI could strengthen state-backed hackers.

items.title: OpenAI slashes funding target by $10 billion amid tech rout, FT reports
items.blurb: OpenAI now seeks about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation after some investors trimmed their allocations.

items.title: The AI trade's trick-or-treat earnings season
items.blurb: Big Tech earnings left investors weighing AI spending risks after a rough October for the Nasdaq.

items.title: OpenAI pares fundraising goal, now seeking up to $20 billion in latest round
items.blurb: OpenAI's lower target and valuation show the tech selloff reaching private AI funding; the round remains open.

items.title: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP suit over data center pollution
items.blurb: A federal judge let a Clean Air Act suit proceed over 27 unpermitted gas turbines powering Memphis-area AI data centers.

items.title: AI data center backlash shapes 2026 midterm elections
items.blurb: Voters in 10 states decide 41 data center ballot measures, turning the AI buildout into a midterm issue.

items.title: Data centers fuel $173 million midterm ad war
items.blurb: Campaigns spent $173 million on mostly negative data center ads, showing how local opposition became a national election issue.

items.title: Foxconn hopes to own 50% of the global AI server market within a couple years
items.blurb: Foxconn's chairman says AI server capacity is fully booked for at least 18 months as demand stays strong.

items.title: Amazon, Intel shares fall after earnings amid AI spending concerns
items.blurb: Disappointing quarterly results hit both stocks, deepening investor doubts about whether heavy AI spending will pay off.

items.title: Musk and Zuckerberg echo Trump's push to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' on earnings calls. Others do not
items.blurb: Musk and Zuckerberg adopted the White House's preferred term; Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet kept saying AI.

items.title: Big Tech bonds, not stocks, offer more opportunity right now, says Bank of America
items.blurb: Borrowing for AI has pushed yields as high as 8% for some investment-grade hyperscalers.

items.title: AI stocks sell off as investors question AI spending returns
items.blurb: Chipmakers led a broad tech decline as investors doubted that heavy AI spending will pay off.

items.title: The big questions remaining after Anthropic's blockbuster IPO prospectus
items.blurb: Anthropic's filing shows $16.29 billion in first-half revenue, slowing growth and founders holding majority voting power.

items.title: Midterms, Apple earnings, jobs report. Wall Street faces a big week ahead just as investors dump tech
items.blurb: Investors head into the Nov 2 week weighing midterms and Apple results after dumping tech shares.

items.title: S&P moves Meta's credit outlook to negative on capex and cash flow
items.blurb: S&P kept Meta's AA- rating but questioned its AI payoff after the company's first negative free cash flow.

items.title: Tech giants need legacy businesses to grow as they pour trillions into the AI buildout
items.blurb: Ads, software and retail still fund the buildout, and only Microsoft kept free cash flow positive last quarter.
